results.notes: I computed the determinant by performing row swaps and Gaussian elimination to upper triangular form, then multiplied the diagonal entries. Two additional row swaps resulted in a net sign of +1, giving the final integer determinant as 8102.

I performed Gaussian elimination to an upper triangular matrix, keeping track of row operations. After swapping two rows, the product of the diagonal entries gave the determinant as 292, then applying the sign change yields -292.
Performed Gaussian elimination to upper triangular form after one row swap, then computed the product of diagonal entries as -2804, and accounted for the sign change to get 2804.

Computed the determinant using Bareiss algorithm (fraction-free Gaussian elimination) on the 6x6 integer matrix step by step, obtaining an upper triangular form and product of pivots resulting in 1248.
Computed determinant via Gaussian elimination to block upper triangular form, then evaluated the resulting 3×3 determinant with rational arithmetic, yielding -7050.
Computed determinant via cofactor expansion along first row, then computed two 5x5 determinants by further expansion into 4x4 and 3x3 matrices, yielding final integer result 4635.

Computed the determinant using row swaps and Gaussian elimination with fractional arithmetic to an upper triangular form. The product of the diagonal entries, accounting for a row swap, gave the result -816.

Performed Gaussian elimination with row swaps and row addition operations (no scaling) to obtain an upper triangular matrix, then computed the product of diagonal entries as -636, accounting for the row swap giving determinant 636.

I performed Gaussian elimination with row swaps to triangularize the matrix, then multiplied diagonal entries. After accounting for two row swaps (net sign +1) and simplifying fractions, the determinant is -3584.
Computed determinant via Laplace expansion along first column, then computed three 5x5 determinants using row reduction and further expansion, resulting in 1388.
